description: Independence rules. Everything is a { value, label } pair: value is the stable key used by logic and stored data and never changes; label is the text people see and can be renamed freely. Treatments and relationships are defined once below and rules refer to them by value. Close affiliates carry one relationship per tree relationship (CA - Ultimate Parent and so on), so each can be treated differently. A relationship's phrase is the plain-language wording used in the independence decision. Each rule lists, per treatment, the service lines it applies to and the tree relationships (measured from an audit client) that inherit it. Where a relationship falls under more than one treatment, the treatment listed first in 'treatments' wins, so keep it ordered strictest first. The wizard embeds a copy of this file (without the prose fields) and reads every rule, label and relationship from it. Service line scoping and the Exempt treatment are defined here but not yet read by the wizard, so its embedded copy has not been updated for them.
serviceLinesNote: A treatment's serviceLines lists the service lines it applies to, by value from the 'serviceLines' catalog below. Three forms: ["*"] is every service line; a value ending in * is a prefix match, so "AUD*" is every AUD- service line and "TAX*" is every TAX- service line; anything else is one specific value, for example "ADV-200". They can be mixed in one list. Exempt is the least strict treatment but wins for its own service lines, so within a rule it is listed first: a relationship that would be restricted or need a materiality check is exempt for those services. A rule may list the same treatment more than once, each entry with its own serviceLines and inheritingRelationships (for example Restricted for TAX* on one set of relationships and Restricted for ADV-200 on another). For a given service line and relationship, the first matching explicit entry wins. The value "default" can be used as a service line: such an entry applies to a relationship only when no explicit entry in the same rule matches that service line and relationship, so it means anything not mentioned. For example Restricted with ["default"] on immediateSubsidiary restricts every service line that no other entry names for immediate subsidiaries. If nothing matches, including a default entry, that relationship is out of scope. The wizard does not ask for a service line yet.
